findings.claim: The new early `return null` when `suppressSourceGeneration is true` runs right after the attribute arguments are read. That is before any member, key or accessibility analysis, so for an opted-out type the collector never reaches the code that reports MsgPack004/005/015/003/012. The fix hides all analyzer diagnostics for `SuppressSourceGeneration = true` types instead of restoring them. This is the opposite of the requirement ('the MessagePack analyzer still reports its diagnostics (MsgPack0xx rules)') and of the 3.1.0 behaviour. Ledger L14 only exempts the generation-only rules MsgPack011/016/017, not 003/004/005/012/015.

receipt_plan.detail: Run Receipts.GeneratedTests.SuppressSourceGenerationAnalyzerTests.SuppressedType_MissingKey_ReportsMsgPack004 and SuppressedType_DuplicateIntKeys_ReportsMsgPack005WithoutCrash on head. Both expect MsgPack004/MsgPack005 for a [MessagePackObject(SuppressSourceGeneration = true)] type and should fail because no diagnostic is produced.

findings.claim: The new README section says the analyzer still validates opted-out types for MsgPack004, 005, 015, 003 and 012. The TypeCollector change returns before any of those checks for such types, so the documentation describes behaviour the code does not have.

receipt_plan.detail: The same tests as the first finding (SuppressedType_MissingKey_ReportsMsgPack004) show that MsgPack004 is not reported for a suppressed type, which contradicts README.md:1625-1630.
